description: Start an interactive program (vim, git rebase -i, npm init, ssh, python, psql, htop, an installer...) in a real terminal and return its screen. Use this instead of the shell tool whenever a command prompts for input, opens an editor or pager, or draws a full-screen UI. The session stays open across calls; drive it with tui_send.

command.description: Command line, run through your shell.

cwd.description: Working directory. Defaults to the server's cwd.

name.description: Optional name to refer to the session by.

wait.description: When to return. Conditions are OR-ed. Without one, the tool waits until the screen stops changing (300 ms quiet), which is fine for most steps; use text/regex/gone for slow programs.

gone.description: Return once this substring is no longer on screen (e.g. a spinner or 'Installing').

idle_ms.description: Return after this long with no output.

regex.description: Return once this JavaScript regex matches the screen.

text.description: Return once this substring is on screen.

timeout_ms.description: Upper bound in ms. Default 5000, max 600000.

name: tui_start
